memory_update.text: USFD should remain in the reference lane as a benchmark for foodservice distribution economics, route density, independent restaurant procurement, and consolidation pressure; not currently an underfollowed Consumer chokepoint candidate without primary-source evidence.

POOL should remain in the reference lane as a benchmark for specialty distributor economics tied to recurring pool maintenance and repair/remodel demand; key falsifiers are discretionary renovation weakness, weather volatility, channel destocking, and new-pool construction exposure.

ITRK.L should remain in the reference lane for consumer-product TIC and retail supply-chain assurance; the potential chokepoint is regulatory/certification workflow stickiness, but consumer mix and growth durability require annual-report validation.

BVI.PA should remain in the reference lane for diversified TIC exposure to consumer-product testing, supply-chain certification, and retail compliance; must be compared directly with Intertek and SGS before any stronger claim.

No primary-source filings or company presentations for USFD, POOL, ITRK.L, or BVI.PA were included in the supplied search context; Layer 2C should pull 10-Ks/annual reports, segment revenue, margin data, customer mix, and management commentary before upgrading any relationship above hypothesis.

This chunk is reference-heavy and does not satisfy the underfollowed discovery lane by itself; later funnel steps should use these references to identify smaller suppliers, route-density specialists, lab/testing niches, software compliance vendors, packaging/labeling providers, and regional distributors.

summary: This Layer 2B chunk is primarily a reference-lane map, not the main underfollowed alpha lane. USFD and POOL are reference distributors for testing foodservice procurement density and repair/remodel maintenance economics. ITRK.L and BVI.PA are reference TIC providers for testing whether rising consumer-product compliance, retailer supplier assurance, tariff/country-of-origin complexity, and food/retail traceability requirements translate into durable inspection/certification demand. Direct evidence for these four tickers remains weak in the supplied search context, so ticker-specific relationships are kept as hypotheses or inferences pending primary-source validation.
